alice_support: ACME reports intermittent 400s when calling our Functions endpoint (JSON mode). They say the same payload works against their local mock but fails on hosted. Attaching example payload and the error they see.

alice_support: ```json
POST /v1/functions/call
{
  "name": "createInvoice",
  "args": {
    "customer_id": "acme-123",
    "line_items": null,
    "metadata": {}
  }
}
```

alice_support: Error snippet from hosted request (customer-provided):
```json
{
  "request_id": "r-02b9f3c4",
  "status": 400,
  "error": "invalid_arguments",
  "message": "args.line_items: expected array<item>, got string"
}
```

sam_engineer: thanks — can you paste the full raw body (not the SDK-logged version)? SDKs sometimes stringify nulls when mixing string interpolation. also need the request_id and the runtime trace id.

alice_support: pasted raw body and headers to the thread. request_id r-02b9f3c4, trace ts 2029-03-11T16:00:12Z. Customer using our JS SDK v1.12.0.

nina_infra: deploy-bot shows api-server v1.42.7 rolled 2h before their failure window. no infra errors in host logs, just the runtime argument validation rejecting the call.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: api-server v1.42.7 -> 1.42.7+hotfix-1 deployed at 2029-03-11T14:01:00Z to prod-a

sam_engineer: I repro locally when I call the hosted endpoint with a raw body where `line_items` is literal `null` but our server-side JSON mode validation goes: if args.value is type string -> try parse JSON -> if parse succeeds treat as stringified payload. In this case the upstream SDK appears to send "null" (string) for null arrays. That yields a string instead of null -> validation fails.

sam_engineer: quick repro curl I used: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions/call \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"name":"createInvoice","args":{"customer_id":"acme-123","line_items":"null"}}'
```

alice_support: customer insists they didn't stringify null manually — they call `args: { line_items: null }` in their code. sdk v1.12.0 change log shows a stringify fallback for older fetch environments.

sam_engineer: two immediate remediation options: (1) SDK patch: ensure we send real JSON nulls for nullable fields (recommended); (2) runtime tolerant mode: treat literal string values equal to "null" or "[]" as their parsed equivalents for parameters declared as array or nullables (backcompat). I prefer SDK fix + short-term runtime tolerant parsing for hosted.

lina_billing: flagged: customer also hit an unexpected 402 BillingRequired for a related retry. billing shows multiple failed attempts counting toward rate/billing checks. we should tell support to advise customer to pause retries until we confirm fix to avoid additional charges.

nina_infra: adding note — if we enable tolerant parsing we must gate it behind a rollout flag for 24-48h and monitor any regression in structured-output callers.

sam_engineer: opened internal PR with runtime patch (parse-lax-null-array) and tests. linking: https://repo.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4578. Patch handles these cases: 
- args declared array -> if value is string and value in ["null","[]"] -> coerce to []
- args declared array nullable -> if value is string "null" -> coerce to null

alice_support: next steps for support: 1) tell customer we've reproduced and working on hotfix; 2) recommend temporary workaround: set `line_items: []` or update SDK to latest pre-release that preserves nulls; 3) pause aggressive retries to avoid billing noise.

sam_engineer: marking this P2 for now since it's reproducible but non-catastrophic. I'll request a canary rollout of the tolerant parser to prod-a only, monitor error rate for createInvoice.

alice_support: thanks — i'll update customer and create an escalation ticket (ESCL-2029-1287) with the request_id and repro curl.

nina_infra: will watch metrics, alert if regression >0.5% for structured-output endpoints in the next 2h.

alice_support: :white_check_mark: closing the thread here once customer confirmed we applied workaround or SDK update.
